newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs light trade, steady-dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs light trade, steady-dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs early Friday sold steady in light trading, with many packers nearly finished buying the hogs they need for weekend operations, livestock dealers said.

Demand was light amid outlooks for light Saturday slaughter as packers continued to fight unprofitable operating margins, they said. Saturday slaughter was estimated by livestock analysts at 20,000 to 30,000 head, compared with 34,000 a week ago and 21,000 a year ago.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hogs sold steady at $56.00-$57.00 in the country and $58.00-$59.00 plants.

Illinois hogs also traded in light volume at steady prices, with $56.50 to $58.00 paid in the country and up to $59.00 at plants, the dealers said. Some plants continued to pay premiums for top quality hogs, with at least one plant reportedly buying hogs at $60.00, they said.

Indiana hogs sold steady at $56.50 to $57.00 in the country and $58.00 to $58.50 at plants. Ohio hogs also traded steady in thin demand at $54.50 to $55.00 in the country and $56.50 to $57.50 at plants.
"We've got good enough demand for the number of hogs we're getting," one Ohio dealer said.
